This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on infrastructure as code so output stays consistent and easy to review.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Check that infrastructure as code terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
2. Measure before optimizing any infrastructure as code bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
3. Before starting infrastructure as code work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
4. When infrastructure as code guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
5. When infrastructure as code decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
6. Validate infrastructure as code outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
7. State assumptions about infrastructure as code explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
8. Document any non-obvious infrastructure as code decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
9. Re-check edge cases relevant to infrastructure as code (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated infrastructure as code concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop infrastructure as code edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not apply generic infrastructure as code advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for infrastructure as code, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
